Group-level cross-validation for brsmm models

Source: R/cv.R
brsmm_cv.Rd

K-fold cross-validation of a brsmm model with folds formed by group: all observations of a group (cluster) are in the same fold. Each held-out group is scored by its marginal log-likelihood at the estimates of the fit to the other folds.

Usage

brsmm_cv(
  formula,
  random = ~1 | id,
  data,
  k = 10L,
  repeats = 1L,
  folds = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  score_points = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula, random

Model and random-effects formulas passed to brsmm.

data

Data frame.

k

Number of folds (default 10).

repeats

Number of repeated k-fold runs (default 1).

folds

Optional fold assignment: a vector named by the group levels (read by name when its unique names are exactly the levels), or else a vector with one fold label per row of data, constant within each group. Overrides k, repeats and seed.

seed

Optional integer seed for the fold assignment.

score_points

Nodes per dimension of the adaptive Gauss-Hermite rule that scores held-out groups; NULL for the default (see Details).

...

Further arguments for brsmm (e.g. ncuts, int_method, n_points, cutpoints).

Value

A data frame of class "brsmm_cv" with one row per fold: repeat, fold, n_groups_train, n_groups_test, n_train, n_test, log_score (sum over the held-out groups), converged, error and warning (messages of the fold fit). Attributes: log_score (total per repeat; NA if a fold failed), group_scores (held-out contribution of each group, one vector per repeat), folds (fold of each group, one vector per repeat, named by group level: integer for drawn folds, the type of the supplied folds otherwise, character for a factor) and score_points.

Details

The held-out log score of a fold is \(\sum_g \log \int \prod_i P(S = s_{gi} \mid b)\, \varphi(b; 0, \hat D)\, db\) over its groups, at the training-fold estimates (brs_loglik_contrib with newdata). The random effects of held-out groups are integrated out, so no random-effect estimates are needed. The integral is computed by adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature with score_points nodes per random-effect dimension, whatever int_method the fits use; the default is 31 for one or two random effects and otherwise the largest number whose product grid has at most 20000 nodes (27 for three, 11 for four, 7 for five; at least 2). The grid may not exceed 500000 nodes. For score data the log score is the log probability of the observed scores (no Jacobian term), so it is on the same scale as the held-out log-likelihood of any model that gives a probability mass function on \(0, \ldots, K\), evaluated on the same folds (attribute "folds").

Rows with missing values in the model variables (response, covariates, random-effect terms or group) are dropped first; a group without complete rows is not used, and n_train / n_test count complete rows.

Folds: k folds of nearly equal numbers of groups, drawn at random for each repeat. With seed, the folds are drawn after set.seed(seed) and the RNG state is restored afterwards; without it, the current RNG state is used. folds gives the assignment directly (one repeat). Held-out rows use the cells of the training fit (its estimated cutpoints under cutpoints = "boundary"). A fold whose fit or scoring fails (for example, a factor level or a border score missing from the training folds) has log_score = NA and the message in error.

See also

brs_cv, brs_loglik_contrib, brsmm

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(21)
nrs <- expand.grid(id = 1:30, time = c("6h", "12h", "24h"))
b0 <- rnorm(30, sd = 0.8)
eta <- -1.3 + c(0, 0.75, 0.3)[nrs$time] + b0[nrs$id]
shp <- brs_repar(mu = plogis(eta), phi = 0.2, repar = 2)
nrs$y <- round(10 * rbeta(nrow(nrs), shp$shape1, shp$shape2))

cv <- brsmm_cv(y ~ time, random = ~ 1 | id, data = nrs, k = 5, seed = 1,
               ncuts = 10)
cv
#>   repeat fold n_groups_train n_groups_test n_train n_test log_score converged
#> 1      1    1             24             6      72     18 -37.84983      TRUE
#> 2      1    2             24             6      72     18 -40.70206      TRUE
#> 3      1    3             24             6      72     18 -39.15762      TRUE
#> 4      1    4             24             6      72     18 -39.61621      TRUE
#> 5      1    5             24             6      72     18 -41.23546      TRUE
#>   error warning
#> 1  <NA>    <NA>
#> 2  <NA>    <NA>
#> 3  <NA>    <NA>
#> 4  <NA>    <NA>
#> 5  <NA>    <NA>
attr(cv, "log_score")
#> [1] -198.5612
# }
